 FOOTBALL OUTLOOK: Region leaders, playoff hopefuls face key tests in week 10
 This is the point in the season, only days from Halloween, that top teams have the most to fear, with the risk of spooks, scares and upsets rising higher and higher each Friday as playoff time gets closer. 
 By Clay Reynolds 
 ● 
 Sports 
 ● 
 October 22, 2026 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 This is the point in the season, only days from Halloween, that top teams have the most to fear, with the risk of spooks, scares and upsets rising higher and higher each Friday as the playoffs get closer. 
 Week 10 in the Heart of Georgia may have some similar potential to the past Saturday in college football, on which no one at the top of the rankings was safe, as several area teams in a share of first place face upstart challengers intent on plunging region title races into some late-season chaos. 
 No. 3 Dublin (6-1, 3-0 region 2-AA) will likely be in for the same type of test it’s faced back-to-back years against Dodge County, which gave the Irish all they wanted by taking leads deep into the second halves of regular season finales in 2024 and ’25 that they’d survive for respective first- and second-place region finishes.

 Turnovers were key pieces in second-half comebacks by Dublin to beat Dodge in both 2024 and 2025, this fumble a major pivot point late in the first half after the Indians took an early two-score lead last fall. The teams will meet for a second-straight year in the Shamrock Bowl Friday night /HORACE AUSTIN, File 
 The Indians (5-3, 2-1 region) are once again positioned to play spoiler as they make a second-straight visit to the Shamrock Bowl hoping to finish the unfinished business left over from both previous campaigns in which big plays from their passing game caused Dublin some major problems. 
 Can the Irish make enough in the other direction to hold them off again, and stay perfect in the region? 
 West Laurens (4-4, 3-1 region 3-AAAA) finds itself on the other side of the same coin as it travels to take on co-league frontrunner Liberty County (5-3, 4-0 region), and hopes to earn some redemption after dropping a winnable opportunity to maintain its earlier spot in first place against Harlem’s just-as-evenly-matched team two weeks ago. 
 A victory, to get the Raiders above .500 for the first time this fall, would keep their chances of contending for the region crown alive. But more important is the likely boost it would carry in GHSA Post Season Rankings that would be critical for a potential jump into the top 16, and their chances of hosting in the first round of the playoffs. 
 With East Laurens idle, Trinity (2-6, 0-3 district) will have Laurens County’s lone other game as it visits Piedmont (2-6, 1-1 district). The Crusaders will be hoping for a more consistent night on offense and defense, and a change in recent fortunes that have them coming in on a four-game losing streak. 
 Trinity’s Tayt Evans extends a stiff arm on a Flint River Academy defender last Friday. The Crusaders will need some more consistency running the ball, and stopping the run, if they hope to end a four-game slide in their next-to-last regular-season game at Piedmont /DANNY SCARBORO 
 In the rest of the area’s action, the biggest matchup will be a last of the regular season for Brentwood (6-3, 3-1 district) at Thomas Jefferson (6-3, 2-2 district), which is yet another local rival its battered squad will be fortunate to make it past. 
 Neighboring Washington County (3-5, 2-2 region 4-AAA) has another big one on its hands as it seeks to get off a two-game slide at Burke County (4-3, 2-1 region). The Golden Hawks need a win to solidify their chances of advancing to the playoffs for a 19th straight year, or else will spend their last week of the regular season on the bubble.
 No. 1 Johnson County (7-0, 3-0 region 5-A), hosting Hancock Central (2-5, 1-2 region), and No. 5 Bleckley County (7-1, 3-1 region 2-AA), entertaining Vidalia (2-5, 0-3 region), will be out to take care of business at home. 
 After being shut out in back-to-back losses, Montgomery County (4-3, 0-1 region 3-A) needs to find some points that may be just as short in supply against the well-tested defense of ECI (3-4, 1-0 region, while Wheeler County (3-4, 2-1 region 4-A) will look to extend its two-game winning streak at winless Wilcox Co. (0-8, 0-4 region), Twiggs County (1-7, 0-4 region 5-A) tries its luck at GMC (3-4, 0-3 region) and Wilkinson County (3-5, 2-2 region 5-A) plays its next-to-last of the regular season at Jenkins County (3-4, 3-0 region). 
 Author
 Clay Reynolds 
 Clay took over the Sports Desk in 2020, but has been with The Courier Herald as a virtual jack of all trades since joining the staff as a student intern in 2010. The Dublin native, a graduate of the University of Georgia’s Grady College of Journalism and Mass Communication, has worked all over the newsroom in a variety of full- and part-time roles and received numerous Georgia Press Association awards for his writing, photography and editing. In addition to reading his area sports coverage, you can also hear him on the radio as a local play-by-play voice, host of 92.7 WKKZ’s “Tailgate Party” and occasional contributor to the Georgia Southern Sports Network.
